transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-06
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Nguyen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Paul Hargreaves (Marleau CTO), Maya Singh (Marleau Head of Ops), Raj Patel (Marleau ML Lead)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Intro + goal: understand cost per inference, tradeoffs hosted vs dedicated vs private, and feasibility of a 1-month pilot.
- Key asks from customer: strict monthly budget cap, on-prem data residency for PII, KMS integration, and latency <= 200ms p95 for chat agent.
- Redwood to send pricing, benchmark plan, and run pilot.

Topics: cost/unit economics, batching & KV cache, quantization options, SLA and residency, pilot scope, security requirements.

Action items (captured quickly): see metadata field.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick intros, and then we'll dive into what your cost constraints look like and how we can map them to hosting options.
[00:22] Paul (CTO): Thanks. I'll keep it short. We're running a logistics assistants prototype that annotates routing exceptions and answers ops questions. Main point: we have a hard monthly spend cap at our wallet for Q1 while we validate. Need to know per-token math and levers.
[00:38] Maya (Ops): And we have strict data residency — anything with PII must stay in our VPC or on-prem. So private hosting is on the table.
[00:49] Raj (ML): From model side, we plan to use a 13B LLM family right now, occasionally 70B for harder prompts. Latency target for the UI is 150-200ms p95.
[01:05] Ethan (SE): Cool. Quick clarifying q: is the 150-200ms target end-to-end from user click to text render, or just inference?
[01:12] Raj: End-to-end ideally, but if you say inference-only 120-140ms is acceptable.
[01:18] Sofia: Great. High level, the levers we look at are: batching (per-request grouping), KV prefix caching, model quantization, and hosting mode — hosted vs dedicated reserved GPU vs private VPC/on-prem. Each affects cost and latency in different ways.
[01:34] Paul: Right, and we care about predictable burn. We can't have wild daily variations.
[01:38] Ethan: That's where Dedicated helps — reserved pools give throughput predictability and lower unit cost, but requires commit. Hosted has lower barrier to entry and flexible scaling but unit price is higher. Private brings residency and control but ops overhead.
[01:57] Maya: Do you do KMS/HSM integration for Private? We need envelope encryption with customer KMS.
[02:03] Sofia: Yes, we support KMS integrations and HSM for keys on Private deployments; for Hosted, we do encryption at rest with our key management but we can discuss bring-your-own-key options for Dedicated or Private.
[02:18] Raj: Can you walk me through how batching interacts with latency? We worry about batching causing user-facing delay.
[02:25] Ethan: Sure — continuous batching groups simultaneous requests to amortize kernel cost. If you set small max-batch and a short aggregation window (e.g., 5-10ms), you get some batching benefits with minimal added tail latency. For chat workloads with lower concurrency, prefix KV cache reduces repeated compute a lot because the model doesn't recompute the conversation history tokens.
[02:44] Raj: KV cash? — sorry, cache, yeah.
[02:46] Ethan: Yeah KV cache. There's also dynamic batching vs fixed batching. Dynamic is better for variable rates.
[02:53] Paul: How do we estimate per-token cost given our usage? We have 1M user messages a month, average 120 tokens in, 240 tokens out.
[03:03] Sofia: Roughly, if you pick Hosted 13B at our standard per-token rate (we gave a baseline in the deck), multiply tokens * rate and add a small overhead for request handling. But important: with batching and KV caching, your effective tokens billed can drop because cached prefix tokens aren't regenerated. Also quantizing a model to int8 or int4 changes GPU throughput and lowers cost per token but can affect quality.
[03:26] Maya: We are very quality-sensitive for certain flows (customer-facing replies) and willing to pay more there, but for internal tooling we want cheap options.
[03:33] Ethan: That's exactly the multi-tier routing use case — route high-SLA traffic to a high-quality model/instance, low-SLA to quantized or smaller model. Redwood supports policy routing by label, region, and cost tier.
[03:45] Raj: Any real numbers — like percent improvement from KV cache or batching in practice?
[03:50] Ethan: In our benchmarks, for chat with long history KV cache saved up to 40-65% of per-request work depending on reuse. Batching in high-concurrency scenarios can reduce per-token GPU cost 15-40% depending on sequence length and model. Combined, customers often see 30-50% reduction in token bill for conversational workloads. But results vary.
[04:09] Paul: That's promising. Our tricky bit is the budget cap — say we have $15k/month for this pilot. Can you help us model tradeoffs?
[04:17] Sofia: Yes. We usually do a quick pilot estimate: you provide sample traffic and we run scenarios (hosted, dedicated reserve, private ops). For $15k, hosted might cover X tokens/month, dedicated requires an estimate of commit to reach lower unit costs. We'll send a spreadsheet showing break-even points.
[04:32] Maya: What about fallback and graceful degradation if capacity spikes? We can't have outages.
[04:38] Ethan: We support automatic fallback to compatible model variants and cross-region routing. For Dedicated we offer burst capacity options (pay-as-you-go on top of reserve) and SLAs. For Private, you'd need to size for peak or enable hybrid fallback to Hosted if the policy allows.
[04:55] Raj: On quantization: have you validated int4 on our 13B stack? We're concerned about hallucination increase.
[05:02] Ethan: We have recommended quant profiles per model family. For many 13B variants int8 gives decent win with minimal quality loss; int4 is more aggressive and we pair it with eval sets. We can run side-by-side quality tests during the pilot to measure delta.
[05:17] Paul: For security compliance, will you provide audit logs and RBAC for Private? We need to show audit trail for SOC 2.
[05:24] Sofia: Yes — Private includes full audit logs, RBAC/SAML integration, and can be configured to retain logs within your VPC. For Hosted we provide audit logs as well but retention windows differ; we can discuss extended retention as an add-on.
[05:39] Paul: Ok. I'm worried about the ops overhead for Private. How much uplift in our team headcount is typical?
[05:45] Ethan: Private requires some infra ops — customers often allocate 0.2-0.5 FTE during ramp for integration and runbooks. We'll provide an operator playbook and scripts to ease upgrades. Dedicated offloads more infra burden to Redwood.
[05:59] Maya: One meta question — how are unit prices calculated for tokens that are generated from cached prefixes? Are those billed?
[06:06] Sofia: Good q. We bill for tokens actually generated by the model. If the runtime pulls from KV cache and doesn't run attention for prefix tokens, you don't get charged for re-evaluating those tokens. However there are engineering edge cases; we'll show exact billing lines in the pricing sheet.
[06:25] Raj: Can you do a quick example on the call with our numbers? 1M messages, 120 in / 240 out, 60% reuse due to repeated context, 20% routed to high-quality 70B model.
[06:36] Sofia: Sure — eyeballing: raw tokens = (1M * (120+240)) = 360M tokens. If 60% of input tokens are served from prefix cache, and outputs have 0% cache, effective billed tokens drop. Let's say effective billed is ~200M tokens. If hosted per-token price is $0.00004 per token (example), that's $8k. If 20% go to 70B at higher rate, add premium. These are illustrative — we'll run precise numbers in the spreadsheet.
[07:05] Paul: That rough number helps. We need the spreadsheet to model dedicated break-even too.
[07:09] Sofia: We'll include break-even: dedicated reserved x months commit vs hosted cost and pilot sensitivity to modal usage and KV cache hit rate.
[07:18] Maya: On residency, for pilot can Dedicated be set up inside our VPC?
[07:23] Ethan: Yes, we offer Dedicated in customer VPCs in selected regions; Private is the full on-prem install if you need air-gapped. For Dedicated in VPC you still get Redwood managed control plane optionally.
[07:36] Raj: On monitoring, what observability do you provide to track token breakdowns by route/model?
[07:42] Sofia: Redwood Console shows token breakdown per-token per-route, latency histograms, per-model cost, and traces for individual requests. We can open a demo console for you in follow-up.
[07:55] Paul: What's typical pilot length and acceptance criteria?
[07:58] Ethan: 2-4 weeks is common for basic pilot with benchmarking. Acceptance: meeting latency and quality thresholds, and validation on cost buckets. For Private, pilot is longer because of deployment.
[08:09] Maya: We also need to involve procurement — legal asks about data processing agreement and liability.
[08:14] Sofia: We'll attach our standard DPA and SOC 2 summary and can run legal review. We can also share a template MSA for dedicated commitments.
[08:24] Raj: Any gotchas with tokenization differences across models — does that affect cost calc?
[08:29] Ethan: Yes tokenization varies by model; our pricing sheets use tokens as measured by the serving model. We'll standardize measurement in the benchmark.
[08:37] Paul: Competitors — we've chatted with OtherCloudAI and did some PoC with InferaSys. How do you differ on pricing transparency?
[08:45] Sofia: We focus on unit economics visibility — console-level per-route token cost and recommendations like which quant or batch settings to use. We also provide model and quantization suggestions per workload.
[08:56] Maya: Any stubs for network ingress/egress cost for Dedicated in our VPC?
[09:01] Ethan: Network costs are usually billed by your cloud provider; Redwood factors some egress estimates into our cost models for Hosted where applicable. For Dedicated in your VPC, we help estimate but don't bill network.
[09:14] Paul: Ok. Can we sketch a pilot scope now so we can get internal approval?
[09:18] Sofia: Sure. Proposed pilot: 2-week benchmark + 2-week validation. Redwood provides a hosted test environment and option for Dedicated trial nodes in your VPC. Objectives: measure p95 latency for critical flows, measure cost per effective token under caching/batching, and run quality A/B of quantized vs baseline. Deliverables: benchmark report, cost model spreadsheet, recommended hosting mode and rollback plan.
[09:44] Raj: Good. What data do you need from us?
[09:46] Ethan: Sample prompts, traffic distribution, target flows with quality labels, and a small set of test queries we can use for eval. Paul mentioned 1M msgs/month; we'll need more shape (peak/concurrency).
[09:56] Paul: I'll pull 3 months logs and anonymize PII.
[09:59] Maya: I'll check on procurement timeline.
[10:02] Sofia: Great. Any final questions?
[10:04] Paul: One last — what's the failure mode if we exceed a budget during pilot? Is there a hard cap?
[10:09] Sofia: For Hosted we can set hard usage caps per account; for Dedicated you'd control bursting policy. We'll make sure to set alerts and a kill switch if you want a hard cap.
[10:18] Maya: Thanks, that's reassuring.
[10:20] Sofia: Thanks everyone — we'll send the pilot proposal and pricing spreadsheet within 72 hours.
[10:25] Ethan: I'll follow up on the benchmark plan and proposed dataset.
[10:28] Paul: Thanks all.
[10:30] End of call.
